message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of the clade **Laurasiatheria**.  
Laurasiatheria is a major group of placental mammals that includes the orders Carnivora (to which lions belong) and Perissodactyla (to which zebras belong). The divergence of these two orders is estimated to have occurred roughly **70–80 million years ago**, so the common ancestor of lion and zebra would have been a small, likely omnivorous mammal living at that time, from which the diverse lineages of carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates later evolved.
